title: Drama
tagline: From Rocky to Magnolia without noticing the water got hot.

levels.name: Popcorn
levels.note: A boxer, a whistleblower, four boys, twelve jurors, Facebook and the Globe.

levels.name: Modern classics
levels.note: A cliff, a lawnmower, runners, erased memories, salesmen and a man mad as hell.

levels.name: Golden age
levels.note: Atticus, Mr. Smith, James Dean, Brando twice, Bette Davis and the Joads.

levels.name: New Hollywood
levels.note: A bank job, fifty eggs, Fast Eddie, Nurse Ratched, a sandwich and a dying town.

levels.name: Heavy
levels.note: Altman, the hottest day in Brooklyn and Jake LaMotta.

core.b: A Philadelphia nobody gets a shot at the heavyweight title. The steps, the raw eggs, 'Adrian!' It's a love story first.

seq.note: Apollo's son, and the best of the later ones

br.note: Two brothers in an MMA tournament
Mickey Rourke's broken-down pro
Indiana kids race bikes against the college boys
Show me the money

core.b: Julia Roberts's foul-mouthed single mum takes on a power company poisoning a town. Soderbergh makes a legal drama feel like a heist.

br.note: Travolta's lawyer against a polluter
Mark Ruffalo against DuPont

core.b: Four boys walk the railway tracks in 1959 to see a dead body. The leeches, the train bridge, the last line.

br.note: O Captain! My Captain!
A teenage Rolling Stone writer on tour with a band
It's not your fault

core.b: One juror (Henry Fonda) talks eleven others out of a guilty verdict in one sweaty room. 96 minutes, no wasted line.

br.note: James Stewart's small-town lawyer, Duke Ellington score
Paul Newman's drunk lawyer gets one last case
The Nazi judges on trial
You can't handle the truth!

core.b: Fincher and Sorkin: Mark Zuckerberg builds Facebook and loses every friend he had. Fast, funny and cold.

br.note: Brad Pitt does baseball with spreadsheets
Sorkin again, three product launches

core.b: The Boston Globe team that uncovered the Church's abuse cover-up. No speeches, just the work, and it's riveting.

br.note: The 2008 crash, explained in a bath
Core on Thriller

core.w: Child abuse is the subject, never shown.

core.b: Two friends' weekend away turns into a run from the law across the Southwest. Brad Pitt's breakout. That ending.
David Lynch's G-rated film: an old man rides a lawnmower 240 miles to make peace with his dying brother. Lovely.

br.note: Lynch, black and white, John Hurt

core.b: Two British runners at the 1924 Olympics, one for God, one against prejudice. The beach run and Vangelis.

br.note: Ken Loach: a Barnsley boy and his kestrel. BFI No. 7
Choose life. BFI No. 10
Shane Meadows' skinheads, 1983
Mike Leigh: a woman finds her birth mother

core.t: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind
core.b: Jim Carrey and Kate Winslet pay to erase each other from memory, and he changes his mind halfway through. Charlie Kaufman's best script.

br.note: Bill Murray in Tokyo
A father and daughter on holiday. It ruins everyone

core.b: Mamet's real-estate salesmen fight over the leads. Baldwin's 'Coffee's for closers', and Pacino, Lemmon, Spacey and Harris at their best.

br.note: Greed is good
One night at a bank before the crash

core.b: Sidney Lumet and Paddy Chayefsky: a TV anchor goes mad on air and the network turns it into a hit. 'I'm as mad as hell!' It predicted everything.

br.note: Wilder's reporter milks a man trapped in a cave
Andy Griffith's drifter becomes a TV demagogue

core.b: Gregory Peck's Atticus Finch defends a Black man in 1930s Alabama, seen through his daughter Scout's eyes.
James Stewart's naive senator takes on a corrupt machine, ending in a one-man filibuster. Capra at his best.

br.note: Capra and Stewart again. Core on Fantasy

core.b: James Dean's troubled new kid, the chickie run and the planetarium. The first teenage film.

br.note: Dean's first starring role
Coppola's black-and-white teen film

core.b: Brando's ex-boxer turned dockworker against the mob union. 'I coulda been a contender.'
Bette Davis's ageing star and the sweet young fan who's after her life. 'Fasten your seatbelts, it's going to be a bumpy night.'

br.note: Burt Lancaster's poisonous columnist. 'Match me, Sidney'
Wilder's alcoholic bender

core.b: Brando's Stanley ('Stella!') and Vivien Leigh's fragile Blanche in a New Orleans tenement. Tennessee Williams at full heat.

br.note: Burton and Taylor tear each other apart

br.t: Cat on a Hot Tin Roof
br.note: Newman and Taylor, Williams again

core.b: John Ford: the Joad family flee the Dust Bowl for California and find no promised land. Henry Fonda's Tom Joad.

br.t: The Best Years of Our Lives
br.note: Three servicemen come home
Ford's Welsh mining family

core.b: Sidney Lumet: Al Pacino's bank robbery goes wrong in an hour and turns into a summer-long media circus. 'Attica! Attica!' Based on a true story, and funnier than you'd expect. Also on Thriller.
Paul Newman's unbreakable chain-gang prisoner. Fifty eggs, and 'What we've got here is failure to communicate.'

br.note: McQueen escapes Devil's Island
Eastwood on the Rock

core.b: Paul Newman's pool shark Fast Eddie takes on Jackie Gleason's Minnesota Fats. Black and white, all smoke and nerve.

seq.note: Scorsese's sequel: Newman mentors Tom Cruise

core.t: One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest
core.b: Jack Nicholson's McMurphy fakes madness to dodge prison and takes on Nurse Ratched. The fishing trip, the Chief.
Jack Nicholson's drifting oil worker, a failed pianist, goes home. The chicken salad sandwich.

br.note: Mrs. Robinson, Simon & Garfunkel and the bus
Jon Voight's hustler and Dustin Hoffman's Ratso
Fonda, Hopper, Nicholson on the road
Wenders' Harry Dean Stanton. Also on World cinema

core.b: Peter Bogdanovich: the last days of a dying Texas town in 1951, in black and white. Jeff Bridges, Cybill Shepherd, Cloris Leachman.

br.note: Paul Newman's heel, also from Larry McMurtry

core.b: Altman's 24 characters over five days of country music and politics, building to a big outdoor concert. Overlapping talk; endlessly rewatchable.

br.note: Altman's Hollywood satire. Core on Comedy
Altman's Raymond Carver LA mosaic

core.b: Spike Lee: the hottest day of the year on one Brooklyn block, and the pizzeria where it boils over. On AFI's and Sight & Sound's lists.

br.note: Spike Lee: Edward Norton's last day before prison
Three ages of one boy in Miami. On Sight & Sound's list

core.b: Scorsese and De Niro's Jake LaMotta: a boxer who destroys everyone who loves him. Black and white, brutal and beautiful.

br.note: A drummer and the teacher from hell
Adam Sandler's 135-minute panic attack

core.b: Orson Welles at 25: the rise and ruin of a newspaper tycoon, told by everyone who knew him. Rosebud. Still the most inventive film ever made.

br.note: Welles's follow-up, butchered by the studio

core.b: Paul Thomas Anderson's three-hour San Fernando Valley mosaic: Tom Cruise's seduction guru, a quiz-show kid and a dying man, all on one rainy day.

br.note: Anderson's 70s porn industry. Good enough to be core

beyond.t: The Passion of Joan of Arc
beyond.b: Carl Dreyer's silent trial of Joan, almost entirely in close-up. Falconetti's face is one of the great performances in film. 9th on Sight & Sound's critics' list.
